newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Brazil's Malan rules out big devaluation - interview.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan rules out big devaluation - interview.

text.p: Brazil's Finance Minister, Pedro Malan, dismissed the possibility of a large devaluation of the real, according to an interview published Monday in the Argentine daily newspaper La Nacion.
"There will be no return to protectionism nor a 'maxidevaluation' of the real - I want to insist on this to my Argentine friends and readers," Malan was quoted as saying.
Many Argentine analysts consider a major devaluation in neighboring Brazil as the biggest threat to the stability of Argentina's economy.

"There exists no serious economist in Brazil or abroad, not even among the critics of our system, that defend the necessity of a devaluation of the real now," said Malan. "Even so, when I open the Argentine newspapers it appears as if the big issue of discussion is this and I have difficulty understanding it because this is not part of our debate."
Malan last November said the government was not considering any modification to the exchange rate mechanism in place, which allows for a gentle devaluation of the real within a predetermined band.
